architect.rationale:
SHAPE: diamond, and it earns it - but it is a CONVERGENT diamond, not a chain, and that distinction is the whole argument.

Why not single-loop: this is 16 new files across three unrelated services plus a health-data redaction that must be got right. That is not one reviewable diff. More importantly the three pieces fail independently - a broken Roam path parser tells you nothing about whether the WHOOP redaction held.

THE RUN-3 TRAP, ANSWERED DIRECTLY. Disjoint file sets are NOT my argument. The test is whether each done_when is checkable with NO sibling merged, and it is, for one structural reason: 'python -m pytest tests/test_NAME.py' imports src.adapters.NAME DIRECTLY as a module. It does not route through REGISTRY, does not need adapters.load(), and therefore does not need any sibling's registration line to exist. Each slice's test is green on its own branch against a tree where the other two adapters are absent files. No slice consumes an artifact any other slice produces - there is no producer/consumer relationship anywhere here, only three parallel producers.

I checked the one thing that could have made that false: tests/test_contract.py:47 test_registry_starts_empty_but_loadable does NOT assert the registry is empty despite its name - it asserts available() returns a list and that an unknown name raises KeyError. Both stay true as adapters are added. So test_contract.py is NOT a fourth shared file and no slice needs to touch it.

THE SHARED FILE (src/adapters/__init__.py). It is a trivial mechanical conflict, not a coupling. Each slice appends one alphabetically-placed line to the REGISTRY dict literal at line 31. Three additive edits to adjacent lines: git will conflict textually, and the resolution is the union, in alphabetical order - github, roam, whoop. Nothing about slice A's line changes what slice B's line should say, which is the definition of mechanical. The integrator resolves it.

WHAT THE INTEGRATOR MUST VERIFY THAT NO INDIVIDUAL REVIEWER COULD: each reviewer sees a branch where exactly ONE registry line exists, so no reviewer can detect a line silently DROPPED during conflict resolution - the classic union-merge loss. Post-merge the integrator must run, from personal-archive/: (1) 'python -m src.cli list' prints exactly three lines, github, roam, whoop; (2) 'python -m pytest -q' is green across the whole suite, the 6 pre-existing tests plus all three new files; (3) adapters.load called on all three names raises nothing, which proves each registered factory resolves to a real module rather than a stale name.

I ALSO REMOVED THE SECOND WOULD-BE SHARED FILE. .env.example needs a ROAM_EXPORT_PATH line, and its dead READWISE_TOKEN line should go. WHOOP_CLIENT_ID/SECRET and GITHUB_TOKEN blocks already exist there, so only Roam needs an edit - I assigned .env.example exclusively to s3 rather than letting three slices touch it. That turns a potential three-way conflict into zero conflicts, at the cost of one arbitrary-looking ownership rule.

THE CONTRACT IS NOT TOUCHED. No slice writes src/schema/record.json or src/record.py, and none needs to: make_record() already accepts an arbitrary payload dict, and all three sources fit source/kind/id/occurred_at/payload without widening anything. If a builder concludes otherwise it must STOP and escalate - that is a gate-level decision, not a builder's.

TWO FACTS THAT CORRECT THE BRIEF, both verified by me, both changing the plan. (1) whoop-med-tracker/raw/v2_activity_workout.json is an EMPTY LIST - 2 bytes, zero records. The brief said all four files hold 2-3 real records; three of them do (cycle 3, recovery 2, sleep 2), workout holds none. So the whoop slice covers three kinds, not four. There is no honest way to ship a workout fixture without inventing one, which fixtures/README.md forbids outright. Workout is on the NOT DOING list. (2) All records across all three usable files carry ONE distinct user_id, so a single synthetic sentinel replaces it everywhere and the redaction check can be an exact-equality assert rather than a fuzzy one.

ON THE REDACTION CHECK BEING SECRET-FREE. The obvious done_when - grep the fixtures for the real user_id - requires writing that identifier into a committed test or into this state file. state.json lives under graph_agents/, which is a git repo. So the committed check is POSITIVE and structural: assert the sentinel is present, and assert every score float has at most 1 decimal place while every real WHOOP score carries 5 to 7. The negative grep is specified as a reviewer action, with the literal named by reference rather than by value.

WHAT THIS DESIGN DOES NOT PROVE, stated plainly rather than papered over: the decimal-place rule fails closed on floats and on _milli integers, but small integer leaves under score - average_heart_rate, max_heart_rate, sleep_cycle_count, disturbance_count - are indistinguishable from synthetic replacements by any mechanical rule. The instruction is that they be replaced too; only the reviewer's eyes can confirm they were. The whoop reviewer must be told this explicitly, because a green test there means the checkable part is clean, not that all health data is gone.

AMBIGUITY WORTH A DECISION, NOT A BUILD: the Roam fixture. 'Record from a real response, then freeze' (fixtures/README.md) and 'never commit private content' pull in opposite directions when the response IS the user's private notebook. Reading A: commit a faithful excerpt with real block text, maximum fidelity. Reading B: commit a shape-faithful excerpt with every block string synthesised. I RECOMMEND B and planned B - it is exactly the ruling the human already made for WHOOP, and notes are more sensitive than heart rates, not less. Flagging it because it is a fidelity concession the human has not been asked about for this specific source.

PARALLEL_SAFE is true with one gating condition: s3-roam must not be dispatched until the Roam export file exists and its path has been handed to the builder. s1 and s2 have every input they need on disk right now.
